items.title: The pullback functor on descent data for schemes is fully faithful when the covering is fpqc over the same base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: In the situation where descent data for schemes relative to a morphism X to S are compared along a morphism X' to X, the lemma asserts that the pullback functor is fully faithful provided that the single morphism X' to X is an fpqc covering and the base is unchanged (statement lines 8777-8787). Faithfulness is immediate from the surjectivity and flatness of the morphism together with the preceding lemma, so the substance is the essential surjectivity on morphisms (proof lines 8790-8792). Given a morphism of descent data over X', one has to produce a morphism of descent data over X pulling back to it, and this takes three separate steps. The first is a pointwise computation: the two composites from the fibre product of the source with itself over the source to the target agree, which the author proves by chasing scheme points through the two descent isomorphisms, writing the descent isomorphism on points, transporting the points along the given morphism of descent data and concluding that the two images agree after applying the second descent isomorphism, which is legitimate because that isomorphism is invertible (proof lines 8813-8852). The author explicitly advises the reader to prove this step rather than read it, which signals that it is not a formal consequence of the definitions. The second step is the descent of the morphism itself, which uses that the base change of the source along the covering is an fpqc covering and that fpqc coverings are universal effective epimorphisms, so that the morphism over X' factors through a unique morphism over X (proof lines 8855-8863). The third step closes the argument for morphisms of descent data rather than merely morphisms of schemes: the relevant square commutes because after base change to the fibre product of X' with itself over S it commutes, and the morphism between the two fibre products is surjective and flat, so that base change along it is faithful (proof lines 8863-8875). The claim is H3: three independent mechanisms -- a pointwise calculation, a descent along an effective epimorphism, and a faithfulness test after base change -- are needed, and the first of them is the kind of step the author himself flags as non-obvious.
